offer.title: Three steps, in the order that works
offer.subtitle: You can start at any of them. Most of the time, they follow on from each other.

formation.name: Training
formation.pitch: You and your teams, self-sufficient with AI in a few sessions — on your real work, not on demo examples.

conseil.name: Finding use cases
conseil.pitch: A short diagnosis that separates what pays off from what merely looks good in a meeting, with numbers attached.

implementation.name: Implementation
implementation.pitch: From a validated idea to a working tool, plugged into your existing data and processes.

formation.title: Training your teams on AI
formation.lead: Training that starts from your work, not from a catalogue. We use your documents, your emails, your processes — and you leave with habits, not notes.
points: Small-group or one-to-one sessions, on site or remote.
Getting to grips with the main assistants: what they can do, and above all what they cannot.
Writing effective instructions, checking answers, spotting plausible-sounding mistakes.
Confidentiality ground rules: which data may leave the building, and which never may.

conseil.title: Finding the use cases that matter
conseil.lead: AI can do anything, which means it does nothing in particular. The work is choosing: a handful of high-return uses, sifted from the dozens that cost more than they return.
points: Short interviews with the people doing the work, not only with management.
A map of repetitive tasks and what they really cost in time.
Selection of high-return uses, with an estimate of both gain and effort.
A roadmap ordered by payoff — including what you should decline to do.

implementation.title: Implementing the solution
implementation.lead: A validated use case is worth nothing until it is in your teams' hands. This is where it gets built, connected and put into production.
points: Building the tool or integrating an existing one, whichever costs less.
Connecting to your current data and tools, without replacing everything.
A human check where mistakes are expensive, full automation where they are not.
Handover of skills, so you are not dependent on me afterwards.

why.title: Twenty years on the ground, not a brochure
why.lead: I spent twenty years designing and running systems for large organisations. AI doesn't change the method: understand the actual work, target what pays off, ship something that holds up. I work alone, which means the person listening to you is the person building.

proofs.detail: A handful of well-chosen uses produce most of the gain. For the rest, I'll tell you not to bother.
On site and in person when it helps. I know the local fabric and its constraints.
If I can't explain a technical choice in two sentences, it's probably a bad one.
The goal is that you stop needing me, not that you sign a subscription.

contact.title: A project, a question, a doubt?
contact.lead: Write me two lines about what you're trying to do. I'll reply, and I'll tell you straight if I'm the right person.
